proposed_actions: For discount review, use the following gross-product arithmetic: $58 list price − $22 unit cost = $36 gross spread per unit; at full list price for 20 units, revenue would be $1,160, recorded unit cost $440, and gross spread $720. Gross spread as a share of list revenue is $720 ÷ $1,160 ≈ 62.1%.

Under the simplifying assumption that the recorded unit cost applies to all units and excludes overhead and other expenses, $22 per unit is the arithmetic break-even price floor: at that price the gross spread is $0. It implies a maximum discount of $36 per unit, or $720 total (about 62.1% off list), before gross spread turns negative. This is not a recommended or approved discount.

Stock is short by 12. If those units could be acquired at the recorded $22 cost, the conditional cost would be 12 × $22 = $264; the $3,400 checking balance is greater than that amount, but this does not establish that funds are uncommitted or authorize a purchase.
Any discount exception or replenishment purchase requires human approval. Do not commit to fulfillment until replenishment source/timing and vendor eligibility are verified.
